content.text:
I have now reviewed the entire agreement (all five sections, paragraphs p0000–p0074) and every parity-style provision.

**Findings on direction:**
- **p0013 (§1.8)** — the only "no less favorably" parity language: *HDI* must promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than its own catalog titles. This runs **in our favour** (vendor-side parity), so per the detection guidance it is not flagged.
- **p0019–p0022 (§3 Fees; Payment)** — flat 30% of Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold; no most-favoured-customer, best-pricing, or third-party-matching mechanic burdening the Company.
- **p0044 (§7.1)** — reciprocal cross-promotion "on a reciprocal and equitable basis"; a mutual marketing covenant, not an obligation to extend HDI any better terms given to third parties.
- **p0037 (§6.1)** — an exclusivity/non-compete restriction on the Company, not an MFN (and it belongs to a separate rule, so no double-flagging here).
- Word-level searches for "favorably", "third party", MFN/best-price/match language surface nothing else.

No provision obliges the Company to offer HDI terms no less favourable than those given to others or to match third-party offers, so the preferred position is satisfied and no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 1.8 HDI agrees that it shall promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than it promotes HDI's
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on the Company. The only parity ("no less favorably") covenant is §1.8 at p0013, which binds HDI to promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than its own catalog titles — a vendor-side obligation running in our favour, which the playbook welcomes and directs us not to redline. The fee provisions (§3.1–3.4, p0019–p0022) set a fixed 30% share of Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold with no most-favoured-customer, best-pricing or third-party-matching mechanic, and §7.1 (p0044) is a mutual cross-promotion covenant on a "reciprocal and equitable basis", not an obligation to extend HDI any better terms granted to third parties. The Company-side restriction in §6.1 (p0037) is exclusivity/non-compete, not MFN, and is not flagged here to avoid double-counting the same commercial term. This therefore sits at the preferred position (no Customer MFN), not merely the fallback, and no change is needed.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
